source_text: Hence, characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the processes that are basic to taxonomy.
features: Characterisation
Identification
Classification
Nomenclature

source_text: Other universal rules of nomenclature are as follows: 1. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics... 2. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet. 3. Both the words... when handwritten, are separately underlined... 4. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.
features: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics.
The first word represents the genus; the second is the specific epithet.
When handwritten, both words are underlined separately.
The genus name starts with a capital letter, and the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

source_text: Taxonomical studies of all known organisms have led to the development of common categories such as kingdom, phylum or division (for plants), class, order, family, genus and species.
features: Kingdom
Phylum or Division
Class
Order
Family
Genus
Species

source_text: The main criteria for classification used by him [R.H. Whittaker] include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
topic: Criteria for Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification
features: Cell structure
Body organisation
Mode of nutrition
Reproduction
Phylogenetic relationships

source_text: Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape: the spherical Coccus (pl.: cocci), the rod-shaped Bacillus (pl.: bacilli), the comma-shaped Vibrium (pl.: vibrio) and the spiral Spirillum (pl.: spirilla).
topic: Classification of Bacteria based on Shape
features: Coccus (spherical)
Bacillus (rod-shaped)
Vibrium (comma-shaped)
Spirillum (spiral)

source_text: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions. These bacteria are special since they live in some of the most harsh habitats such as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles) and marshy areas (methanogens).
features: Have a different cell wall structure allowing survival in extreme conditions.
Halophiles: live in extreme salty areas.
Thermoacidophiles: live in hot springs.
Methanogens: live in marshy areas and are responsible for methane production.

source_text: In this book we include Chrysophytes, Dinoflagellates, Euglenoids, Slime moulds and Protozoans under Protista.
features: Chrysophytes
Dinoflagellates
Euglenoids
Slime moulds
Protozoans

source_text: There are four major groups of protozoans. Amoeboid protozoans... Flagellated protozoans... Ciliated protozoans... Sporozoans...
features: Amoeboid protozoans (e.g., Amoeba, Entamoeba)
Flagellated protozoans (e.g., Trypanosoma)
Ciliated protozoans (e.g., Paramoecium)
Sporozoans (e.g., Plasmodium)

source_text: The sexual cycle involves the following three steps: (i) Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes called plasmogamy. (ii) Fusion of two nuclei called karyogamy. (iii) Meiosis in zygote resulting in haploid spores.
topic: Steps in the Fungal Sexual Cycle
features: Plasmogamy (fusion of protoplasms)
Karyogamy (fusion of nuclei)
Meiosis (in the zygote to form haploid spores)

source_text: The morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies form the basis for the division of the kingdom [Fungi] into various classes.
features: Morphology of the mycelium
Mode of spore formation
Fruiting bodies

source_text: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. The algal component is known as phycobiont and fungal component as mycobiont, which are autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner.
features: Symbiotic association between algae (phycobiont) and fungi (mycobiont).
Phycobiont is autotrophic and prepares food.
Mycobiont is heterotrophic and provides shelter, water, and mineral absorption.
They are very good pollution indicators.

source_text: In addition to proteins, viruses also contain genetic material, that could be either RNA or DNA. No virus contains both RNA and DNA. ... In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA and viruses that infect animals have either single or double stranded RNA or double stranded DNA. Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages... are usually double stranded DNA viruses.
features: Genetic material is either DNA or RNA, never both.
Plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA.
Animal viruses can have single-stranded RNA, double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA.
Bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) usually have double-stranded DNA.

source_text: The algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.
features: Chlorophyceae (Green algae)
Phaeophyceae (Brown algae)
Rhodophyceae (Red algae)

source_text: The members of chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae... due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b... The food is stored in the form of starch... The cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.
features: Commonly called Green algae.
Major pigments are Chlorophyll a and b.
Stored food is starch.
Cell wall is made of an inner cellulose layer and outer pectose layer.

source_text: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae... possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls... Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol... The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin.
features: Commonly called Brown algae.
Major pigments are Chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin (a xanthophyll).
Stored food is laminarin or mannitol.
Cell wall has cellulose and an outer coating of algin.

source_text: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin... They possess chlorophyll a, d and phycoerythrin... The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
features: Commonly called Red algae.
Major pigments are Chlorophyll a, d, and r-phycoerythrin.
Stored food is floridean starch.
Asexual reproduction by non-motile spores and sexual reproduction by non-motile gametes.

source_text: Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte.
features: Called amphibians of the plant kingdom.
Dependent on water for sexual reproduction.
The dominant phase of the life cycle is the gametophyte.
The main plant body is haploid.

source_text: The pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).
features: Psilopsida (e.g., Psilotum)
Lycopsida (e.g., Selaginella, Lycopodium)
Sphenopsida (e.g., Equisetum)
Pteropsida (e.g., Dryopteris, Pteris)

source_text: The gymnosperms (gymnos : naked, sperma : seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. The seeds that develop post-fertilisation, are not covered, i.e., are naked.
features: Ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall.
Ovules remain exposed.
Seeds that develop after fertilization are naked (not covered).
They include medium-sized trees, tall trees, and shrubs.

source_text: fundamental features common to various individuals in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems. These features are used as the basis of animal classification...
features: Levels of Organisation (cellular, tissue, organ, organ system)
Symmetry (asymmetrical, radial, bilateral)
Nature of Coelom (acoelomate, pseudocoelomate, coelomate)
Patterns of digestive, circulatory and reproductive systems
Segmentation
Presence or absence of Notochord

source_text: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic animals, e.g., coelenterates. Those animals in which the developing embryo has a third germinal layer, mesoderm, in between the ectoderm and endoderm, are called triploblastic animals (platyhelminthes to chordates).
features: Diploblastic animals have two germ layers: ectoderm and endoderm.
Example of diploblastic animals: Coelenterates (Cnidaria).
Triploblastic animals have three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
Examples of triploblastic animals: Platyhelminthes to Chordates.

source_text: The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom. Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods... In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm... Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g., aschelminthes. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes.
features: Coelomates: Possess a true coelom lined by mesoderm (e.g., Annelids, Chordates).
Pseudocoelomates: Possess a pseudocoelom where the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm (e.g., Aschelminthes).
Acoelomates: Do not have a body cavity (e.g., Platyhelminthes).

source_text: Animals belonging to phylum Chordata are fundamentally characterised by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
features: Presence of a notochord.
Presence of a dorsal hollow nerve cord.
Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits.

source_text: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have an elongated body bearing 6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration. Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.
features: Ectoparasites on some fishes.
Have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws (Agnatha).
Body is devoid of scales and paired fins.
Possess 6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration.

source_text: In majority of the dicotyledonous plants, the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of primary root which grows inside the soil. It bears lateral roots of several orders that are referred to as secondary, tertiary, etc. roots. The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system... In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system... In some plants, like grass, Monstera and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious roots.
topic: Types of Root Systems in Plants
features: Tap root system: Primary root develops from the radicle and has lateral branches; characteristic of dicots.
Fibrous root system: Primary root is short-lived and replaced by roots originating from the base of the stem; characteristic of monocots.
Adventitious root system: Roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle (e.g., stem, leaves).

source_text: The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap... A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity... The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement... This region is called the region of elongation... this zone, proximal to region of elongation, is called the region of maturation. From this region some of the epidermal cells form very fine and delicate, thread-like structures called root hairs.
features: Root Cap: A thimble-like structure that covers and protects the root apex.
Region of Meristematic Activity: Area just above the root cap with small, thin-walled, actively dividing cells.
Region of Elongation: Area proximal to the meristematic region where cells undergo rapid elongation and enlargement, responsible for root growth in length.
Region of Maturation: Area where cells differentiate and mature; root hairs arise from this region.

source_text: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch. This is usually of three types – alternate, opposite and whorled... In alternate type... a single leaf arises at each node... In opposite type, a pair of leaves arise at each node and lie opposite to each other... If more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl, it is called whorled.
features: Alternate: A single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner (e.g., china rose).
Opposite: A pair of leaves arises at each node, opposite to each other (e.g., Calotropis, guava).
Whorled: More than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl (e.g., Alstonia).

source_text: The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary... When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping... it is said to be valvate... If one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on... it is called twisted... If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction... the aestivation is called imbricate... In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary.
features: Valvate: Sepals or petals in a whorl just touch at the margins without overlapping (e.g., Calotropis).
Twisted: One margin of an appendage overlaps the next one in a regular direction (e.g., china rose).
Imbricate: Margins overlap but not in any particular direction (e.g., Cassia).
Vexillary (Papilionaceous): The largest petal (standard) overlaps two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap two anterior petals (keel) (e.g., Pea, bean).

source_text: The placentation are of different types namely, marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central and free central... In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture... In axile placentation, the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary... In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part... In free central placentation, the ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent... In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached to it.
features: Marginal: Placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary (e.g., pea).
Axile: Placenta is axial and ovules are attached in a multilocular ovary (e.g., china rose, tomato, lemon).
Parietal: Ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on the periphery (e.g., mustard).
Free Central: Ovules are borne on a central axis, and septa are absent (e.g., Dianthus, Primrose).
Basal: Placenta develops at the base of the ovary with a single ovule attached (e.g., sunflower, marigold).

source_text: On the basis of their structure and location, there are three types of tissue systems. These are the epidermal tissue system, the ground or fundamental tissue system and the vascular or conducting tissue system.
topic: Types of Tissue Systems in Plants
features: Epidermal tissue system
Ground (fundamental) tissue system
Vascular (conducting) tissue system

source_text: Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped... The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called stomatal apparatus.
features: Stomatal aperture (pore).
Guard cells (two), which are bean-shaped in dicots and dumb-bell shaped in grasses.
Subsidiary cells (surrounding the guard cells).

source_text: When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii, the arrangement is called radial such as in roots. In conjoint type of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius... common in stems and leaves. In dicotyledonous stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem... called open vascular bundles. In the monocotyledons, the vascular bundles have no cambium... referred to as closed.
features: Radial: Xylem and phloem are on different radii in an alternating pattern (found in roots).
Conjoint: Xylem and phloem are situated at the same radius (found in stems and leaves).
Conjoint Open: A cambium is present between xylem and phloem (characteristic of dicot stems).
Conjoint Closed: Cambium is absent between xylem and phloem (characteristic of monocot stems).

source_text: The anatomy of the monocot root is similar to the dicot root in many respects... As compared to the dicot root which have fewer xylem bundles, there are usually more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles in the monocot root. Pith is large and well developed. Monocotyledonous roots do not undergo any secondary growth.
topic: Key Differences between Dicot and Monocot Roots
features: Number of Xylem Bundles: Dicot roots are typically diarch to tetrarch (2-4), while monocot roots are polyarch (more than six).
Pith: Dicot roots have a small or inconspicuous pith, while monocot roots have a large, well-developed pith.
Secondary Growth: Dicot roots undergo secondary growth, while monocot roots do not.

source_text: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue... Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones. The phloem parenchyma is absent, and water-containing cavities are present...
topic: Anatomical Features of a Monocot Stem
features: Hypodermis is sclerenchymatous.
Vascular bundles are scattered.
Each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.
Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.
Phloem parenchyma is absent.
Water-containing cavities are present in vascular bundles.

source_text: You may be surprised to know that all complex animals consist of only four basic types of tissues. These tissues are organised in specific proportion and pattern to form an organ...
topic: Four Basic Types of Animal Tissues
features: Epithelial tissue
Connective tissue
Muscular tissue
Neural tissue

source_text: Cell theory as understood today is: (i) all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells. (ii) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
features: All living organisms are composed of cells and their products.
All cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).

source_text: Besides the nucleus, the eukaryotic cells have other membrane bound distinct structures called organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the golgi complex, lysosomes, mitochondria, microbodies and vacuoles. The prokaryotic cells lack such membrane bound organelles.
features: Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)
Golgi complex
Lysosomes
Mitochondria
Microbodies
Vacuoles

source_text: The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system.
features: Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)
Golgi complex (Golgi apparatus)
Lysosomes
Vacuoles

source_text: Based on the type of pigments plastids can be classified into chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts. The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll... The chromoplasts, fat soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls... The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids... Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch),... elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.
features: Chloroplasts: Contain chlorophyll and carotenoids for photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts: Contain fat-soluble carotenoids (carotene, xanthophylls) giving yellow, orange, or red color.
Leucoplasts: Colorless plastids for nutrient storage.
Amyloplasts (a type of leucoplast): Store starch.
Elaioplasts (a type of leucoplast): Store oils and fats.
Aleuroplasts (a type of leucoplast): Store proteins.

source_text: Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere... The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle... In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end... the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.
topic: Types of Chromosomes based on Centromere Position
features: Metacentric: Centromere in the middle, forming two equal arms.
Sub-metacentric: Centromere slightly away from the middle, forming one shorter and one longer arm.
Acrocentric: Centromere situated close to one end, forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
Telocentric: Centromere at the terminal end.

source_text: The acid insoluble fraction, has only four types of organic compounds i.e., proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids. These classes of compounds with the exception of lipids, have molecular weights in the range of ten thousand daltons and above... are called macromolecules or biomacromolecules.
features: Proteins
Nucleic Acids
Polysaccharides
Lipids (found in the acid-insoluble fraction due to membrane association, but are not strictly macromolecules by weight)

source_text: There are four levels. The sequence of amino acids... is called the primary structure... the protein thread is folded in the form of a helix... called the secondary structure... the long protein chain is also folded upon itself like a hollow woolen ball, giving rise to the tertiary structure... Some proteins are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or subunits... called the quaternary structure.
features: Primary Structure: The linear sequence of amino acids.
Secondary Structure: Local folding of the polypeptide chain into structures like alpha-helices and beta-sheets.
Tertiary Structure: Overall 3D folding of a single polypeptide chain.
Quaternary Structure: The arrangement of multiple polypeptide chains (subunits) in a multi-subunit protein.

source_text: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase, M Phase (Mitosis phase). The interphase is divided into three further phases: G1 phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis), G2 phase (Gap 2).
features: Interphase (G1, S, G2)
M Phase (Mitosis and Cytokinesis)

source_text: Karyokinesis involves following four stages: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.
features: Prophase
Metaphase
Anaphase
Telophase

source_text: Prophase I: Prophase of the first meiotic division... has been further subdivided into the following five phases... Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis.
features: Leptotene
Zygotene
Pachytene
Diplotene
Diakinesis

source_text: A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is... due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green...), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange).
topic: Major Photosynthetic Pigments in Green Plants
features: Chlorophyll a
Chlorophyll b
Xanthophylls
Carotenoids

source_text: Light reactions or the 'Photochemical' phase include light absorption, water splitting, oxygen release, and the formation of high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH.
topic: Key Events of the Light-Dependent Reactions
features: Light absorption by pigments.
Splitting of water (photolysis).
Release of oxygen.
Formation of ATP (photophosphorylation).
Formation of NADPH.

source_text: The important steps in the process of decomposition are fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation.
topic: Steps in the Process of Decomposition
features: Fragmentation
Leaching
Catabolism
Humification
Mineralisation

source_text: The period of growth is generally divided into three phases, namely, meristematic, elongation and maturation.
features: Meristematic phase (cell division)
Elongation phase (cell enlargement)
Maturation phase (cell differentiation)

source_text: The PGRs can be broadly divided into two groups... One group of PGRs are involved in growth promoting activities... e.g., auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins. The PGRs of the other group play an important role in... growth inhibiting activities... The PGR abscisic acid belongs to this group. The gaseous PGR, ethylene, could fit either of the groups, but it is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.
features: Growth Promoters: Auxins, Gibberellins, Cytokinins.
Growth Inhibitors: Abscisic acid, Ethylene.

source_text: Respiration involves the following steps: (i) Breathing or pulmonary ventilation... (ii) Diffusion of gases (O2 and CO2) across alveolar membrane. (iii) Transport of gases by the blood. (iv) Diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and tissues. (v) Utilisation of O2 by the cells for catabolic reactions...
features: Breathing (Pulmonary Ventilation)
Diffusion of gases across the alveolar membrane.
Transport of gases by blood.
Diffusion of gases between blood and tissues.
Cellular Respiration (Utilization of O2 by cells).

source_text: Blood is a special connective tissue consisting of a fluid matrix, plasma, and formed elements. Erythrocytes, leucocytes and platelets are collectively called formed elements.
features: Plasma (fluid matrix)
Formed Elements
Erythrocytes (Red Blood Cells)
Leucocytes (White Blood Cells)
Platelets (Thrombocytes)

source_text: We have two main categories of WBCs – granulocytes and agranulocytes. Neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils are different types of granulocytes, while lymphocytes and monocytes are the agranulocytes.
features: Granulocytes: Neutrophils, Eosinophils, Basophils.
Agranulocytes: Lymphocytes, Monocytes.

source_text: The circulatory patterns are of two types – open or closed. Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs... Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system...
features: Open Circulatory System: Blood is pumped into a body cavity (hemocoel). Found in arthropods and molluscs.
Closed Circulatory System: Blood is confined within a network of vessels. Found in annelids and chordates.

source_text: Ammonia, urea and uric acid are the major forms of nitrogenous wastes excreted by the animals... The process of excreting ammonia is Ammonotelism... mainly excrete urea and are called ureotelic animals... excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid... and are called uricotelic animals.
topic: Major Nitrogenous Wastes and Excretion Types
features: Ammonotelism: Excretion of ammonia (e.g., bony fishes, aquatic amphibians).
Ureotelism: Excretion of urea (e.g., mammals, terrestrial amphibians).
Uricotelism: Excretion of uric acid (e.g., reptiles, birds, insects).

source_text: Urine formation involves three main processes namely, glomerular filtration, reabsorption and secretion, that takes place in different parts of the nephron.
features: Glomerular Filtration
Tubular Reabsorption
Tubular Secretion

source_text: Based on their location, three types of muscles are identified : (i) Skeletal (ii) Visceral and (iii) Cardiac.
features: Skeletal Muscle (striated, voluntary)
Visceral Muscle (smooth, involuntary)
Cardiac Muscle (striated, involuntary)

source_text: The axial skeleton comprises 80 bones... The skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs constitute axial skeleton. The bones of the limbs along with their girdles constitute the appendicular skeleton.
features: Axial Skeleton: Includes the skull, vertebral column, sternum, and ribs.
Appendicular Skeleton: Includes the bones of the limbs (arms and legs) and the pectoral and pelvic girdles.

source_text: Joints have been classified into three major structural forms, namely, fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial. Fibrous joints do not allow any movement... cartilaginous joints... permits limited movements. Synovial joints... allows considerable movement.
features: Fibrous Joints (Immovable): e.g., sutures of the skull.
Cartilaginous Joints (Slightly movable): e.g., joints between vertebrae.
Synovial Joints (Freely movable): e.g., knee joint, shoulder joint.

source_text: The human neural system is divided into two parts : (i) the central neural system (CNS) (ii) the peripheral neural system (PNS). The CNS includes the brain and the spinal cord... The PNS is divided into two divisions called somatic neural system and autonomic neural system.
topic: Major Divisions of the Human Neural System
features: Central Nervous System (CNS): Consists of the brain and spinal cord.
Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): Consists of all nerves associated with the CNS.
Somatic Neural System (a division of PNS): Relays impulses to skeletal muscles.
Autonomic Neural System (a division of PNS): Transmits impulses to involuntary organs and smooth muscles.

source_text: The brain can be divided into three major parts: (i) forebrain, (ii) midbrain, and (iii) hindbrain. The forebrain consists of cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus... The hindbrain comprises pons, cerebellum and medulla.
topic: Major Parts of the Human Brain
features: Forebrain: Consists of the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus.
Midbrain
Hindbrain: Consists of the pons, cerebellum, and medulla oblongata.

source_text: Sexual reproduction involves formation of the male and female gametes, either by the same individual or by different individuals of the opposite sex. These gametes fuse to form the zygote which develops to form the new organism.
features: Formation of male and female gametes (Gametogenesis).
Fusion of gametes to form a zygote (Fertilization/Syngamy).
Development of the zygote into a new organism (Embryogenesis).

source_text: Events in sexual reproduction... may be grouped into three distinct stages, namely the pre-fertilisation, fertilisation and the post-fertilisation events.
features: Pre-fertilisation events (Gametogenesis and Gamete Transfer)
Fertilisation events (Syngamy)
Post-fertilisation events (Zygote formation and Embryogenesis)

source_text: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous... The anther is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners, two in each lobe.
topic: Structure of a Typical Angiosperm Anther
features: It is bilobed.
It is dithecous (each lobe has two theca).
It is a four-sided (tetragonal) structure.
It contains four microsporangia.

source_text: The pistil has three parts – the stigma, style and the ovary. The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains. The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary.
features: Stigma: The receptive tip that serves as a landing platform for pollen.
Style: The elongated stalk that connects the stigma and ovary.
Ovary: The basal, swollen part that contains the ovules.

source_text: Since two types of fusions, syngamy and triple fusion take place in an embryo sac the phenomenon is termed double fertilisation, an event unique to flowering plants. The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm while the zygote develops into an embryo.
features: Syngamy: Fusion of one male gamete with the egg cell to form the zygote (diploid).
Triple Fusion: Fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei to form the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) (triploid).
Result: The zygote develops into the embryo, and the primary endosperm cell develops into the endosperm.

source_text: The male reproductive system is located in the pelvis region. It includes a pair of testes alongwith accessory ducts, glands and the external genitalia.
topic: Components of the Male Reproductive System
features: A pair of testes (primary sex organs).
Accessory ducts (rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens).
Accessory glands (seminal vesicles, prostate, bulbourethral glands).
External genitalia (penis).

source_text: The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries alongwith a pair of oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and the external genitalia located in pelvic region.
topic: Components of the Female Reproductive System
features: A pair of ovaries (primary sex organs).
A pair of oviducts (fallopian tubes).
Uterus
Cervix
Vagina
External genitalia (vulva).

source_text: The expression 'reproductive health' simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions. However, it has a broader perspective and includes the emotional and social aspects of reproduction also. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means a total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social.
features: Physical well-being
Emotional well-being
Behavioural well-being
Social well-being

source_text: Mendel proposed that something was being stably passed down, unchanged, from parent to offspring through the gametes, over successive generations. He called these things as 'factors'. Now we call them as genes.
features: Something is stably passed down from parent to offspring.
This 'something' is passed down unchanged through gametes.
He called them 'factors'.
Today, these factors are known as 'genes'.

source_text: Based on his observations on monohybrid crosses Mendel proposed two general rules... Today these rules are called the Principles or Laws of Inheritance: the First Law or Law of Dominance and the Second Law or Law of Segregation.
features: Law of Dominance
Law of Segregation

source_text: Some of the most common chromosomal disorders are Down's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome and Turner's syndrome.
features: Down's syndrome (Trisomy of chromosome 21)
Klinefelter's syndrome (Presence of an additional X chromosome in a male - XXY)
Turner's syndrome (Absence of one X chromosome in a female - XO)

source_text: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group.
features: A nitrogenous base (Purine or Pyrimidine)
A pentose sugar (Ribose or Deoxyribose)
A phosphate group

source_text: The salient features of the Double-helix structure of DNA are as follows: (i) It is made of two polynucleotide chains... (ii) The two chains have anti-parallel polarity... (iii) The bases in two strands are paired through hydrogen-bond (H-bonds)... (iv) The two chains are coiled in a right-handed fashion.
topic: Salient Features of the DNA Double Helix
features: Composed of two polynucleotide chains.
The two chains have anti-parallel polarity (one 5'->3', the other 3'->5').
Bases are paired via hydrogen bonds (A with T, G with C).
The chains are coiled in a right-handed helix.

source_text: Homology indicates common ancestry. Other examples are vertebrate hearts or brains... Analogy refers to a situation exactly opposite... analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution – different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity. e.g., Wings of butterfly and of birds.
features: Homologous Structures: Have a common ancestry and fundamental structure but perform different functions; result of divergent evolution.
Analogous Structures: Have different ancestry and structure but perform similar functions; result of convergent evolution.

source_text: Five factors are known to affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. These are gene migration or gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection.
features: Gene migration (gene flow)
Genetic drift
Mutation
Genetic recombination
Natural selection

source_text: Innate immunity consist of four types of barriers. These are — (i) Physical barriers... (ii) Physiological barriers... (iii) Cellular barriers... (iv) Cytokine barriers...
features: Physical barriers (e.g., Skin, mucus membranes).
Physiological barriers (e.g., Stomach acid, saliva, tears).
Cellular barriers (e.g., Phagocytes like neutrophils, macrophages).
Cytokine barriers (e.g., Interferons).

source_text: The primary lymphoid organs are bone marrow and thymus where immature lymphocytes differentiate into antigen-sensitive lymphocytes. After maturation the lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs like spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix.
features: Primary Lymphoid Organs: Bone marrow, Thymus.
Secondary Lymphoid Organs: Spleen, Lymph nodes, Tonsils, Peyer's patches, Appendix.

source_text: The main sources of biofertilisers are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria.
features: Bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium, Azospirillum, Azotobacter)
Fungi (e.g., Glomus for mycorrhiza)
Cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae, e.g., Anabaena, Nostoc)

source_text: Among many, the two core techniques that enabled birth of modern biotechnology are : (i) Genetic engineering... (ii) Bioprocess engineering...
features: Genetic engineering: Techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA).
Bioprocess engineering: Maintenance of sterile conditions to enable growth of only the desired microbe/cell in large quantities.

source_text: The key tools, i.e., restriction enzymes, polymerase enzymes, ligases, vectors and the host organism.
topic: Key Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology
features: Restriction enzymes (molecular scissors).
Polymerase enzymes (e.g., DNA polymerase).
Ligases (molecular glue).
Vectors (e.g., plasmids, bacteriophages).
Host organism.

source_text: Genetic modification has: (i) made crops more tolerant to abiotic stresses... (ii) reduced reliance on chemical pesticides... (iii) helped to reduce post harvest losses. (iv) increased efficiency of mineral usage by plants... (v) enhanced nutritional value of food...
features: Increased tolerance to abiotic stresses (cold, drought, salt, heat).
Pest resistance, reducing need for chemical pesticides.
Reduction in post-harvest losses.
Increased efficiency of mineral usage.
Enhanced nutritional value (e.g., Vitamin A in Golden Rice).

source_text: The components of the ecosystem are seen to function as a unit when you consider the following aspects: (i) Productivity; (ii) Decomposition; (iii) Energy flow; and (iv) Nutrient cycling.
features: Productivity
Decomposition
Energy flow
Nutrient cycling

source_text: The most important of them are– (i) Genetic diversity... (ii) Species diversity... (iii) Ecological diversity...
features: Genetic diversity: Diversity of genes within a species.
Species diversity: Diversity of species within a region.
Ecological diversity: Diversity of ecosystems in a geographical area.

source_text: There are four major causes ('The Evil Quartet' is the sobriquet used to describe them). (i) Habitat loss and fragmentation... (ii) Over-exploitation... (iii) Alien species invasions... (iv) Co-extinctions...
topic: The 'Evil Quartet' (Major Causes of Biodiversity Loss)
features: Habitat loss and fragmentation
Over-exploitation
Alien species invasions
Co-extinctions

source_text: When we conserve and protect the whole ecosystem, its biodiversity at all levels is protected - we save the entire forest to save the tiger. This approach is called in situ (on site) conservation... when there are situations where an animal or plant is endangered or threatened... and needs urgent measures to save it from extinction, ex situ (off site) conservation is the desirable approach.
features: In situ (on-site) conservation: Protecting species within their natural habitat (e.g., national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves).
Ex situ (off-site) conservation: Protecting species outside their natural habitat (e.g., zoological parks, botanical gardens, seed banks, cryopreservation).

subject: Biology
question: The complex II of mitochondrial electron transport chain is also known as
brief_explanation: In the electron transport chain, Complex II is succinate dehydrogenase, the enzyme that oxidizes succinate to fumarate in the Krebs cycle and transfers electrons to ubiquinone.

subject: Biology
question: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplifies DNA following the equation.
brief_explanation: PCR is a process of exponential amplification of DNA. In each cycle, the amount of DNA doubles. Therefore, after 'n' cycles, the amount of DNA is amplified by a factor of 2ⁿ.

subject: Biology
question: What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method?
statements: A. High fatality risk to mother
B. Expensive instruments and reagents
C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors
D. Less adoption of orphans
E. Not available in India
F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive

options.4: A, B, C, E, F only

brief_explanation: IVF involves expensive procedures (B), can lead to fewer adoptions of orphans (D), and carries a risk of embryo non-survival (F). Fatality risk is not high (A is incorrect), it is available in India (E is incorrect), and donors are not always the husband/wife (C is incorrect).

subject: Biology
question: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
brief_explanation: In frogs, as in humans, the vena cava (specifically, sinus venosus which receives blood from venae cavae) is the major vein that collects deoxygenated blood from the body and delivers it to the right atrium of the heart.

subject: Biology
question: Which one of the following statements refers to Reductionist Biology?

options.1: Physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
options.2: Physiological approach to study and understand, living organisms.
options.3: Chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
options.4: Behavioural approach to study and understand living organisms.

brief_explanation: Reductionist biology is the approach of understanding complex living systems by studying their individual components at a more basic level, such as their physical and chemical properties and interactions.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material... RNA is unstable. Statement II: DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material...

options.1: Both statement I and statement II are correct
options.2: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
options.3: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
options.4: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct

brief_explanation: Both statements are correct. The 'RNA world' hypothesis suggests RNA was the initial genetic material (Statement I). DNA evolved later, offering greater stability due to its double-stranded nature and the use of thymine, making it better for long-term genetic storage (Statement II).

subject: Biology
question: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
brief_explanation: Commensalism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is unaffected (+/0). The epiphyte (like an orchid) gets support and a better position for sunlight, while the mango tree is not significantly harmed or helped.

subject: Biology
question: From the statements given below choose the correct option: A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. B. Each ribosome has two sub-units. C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
statements: D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S.
E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S
brief_explanation: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic are 70S (A is true). Each ribosome has a large and small subunit (B is true). The subunits are 60S and 40S for 80S ribosomes, and 50S and 30S for 70S ribosomes. Svedberg units are not additive (C is true, D and E are false).

subject: Biology
question: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
brief_explanation: Ex-situ conservation involves protecting species outside their natural habitats. Zoos and botanical gardens are prime examples. National parks and wildlife sanctuaries are examples of in-situ conservation.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. Statement II: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP).

options.1: Both statement I and statement II are correct
options.2: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
options.3: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
options.4: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct

brief_explanation: Statement I is correct; the sun is the ultimate source of energy for nearly all ecosystems. Statement II is incorrect; the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is Gross Primary Productivity (GPP). NPP is GPP minus respiratory losses.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Emphysema is characterized by damaged alveolar walls. B-Angina pectoris is acute chest pain from insufficient oxygen to the heart muscle. C-Glomerulonephritis is the inflammation of the glomeruli of the kidney. D-Tetany involves rapid muscle spasms due to low calcium.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statement: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar. Reason (R): The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers.

options.1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.2: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.3: A is true but R is false.
options.4: A is false but R is true.

brief_explanation: Both statements are true. Wind and water-pollinated flowers do not need to attract pollinators, so they are not colorful and lack nectar (Assertion). They produce vast amounts of pollen to compensate for the random nature of dispersal (Reason). However, the reason explains a compensation mechanism, not why the flowers lack attractants. Both are correct but not a direct cause-and-effect explanation.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
brief_explanation: Wine and beer are produced by fermentation without distillation. Whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by fermenting a mash and then distilling it to increase the alcohol concentration.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a floral formula % stands for zygomorphic nature of the flower, and G stands for inferior ovary. Statement II: In a floral formula ⊕ stands for actinomorphic nature of the flower and G stands for superior ovary.

options.1: Both statement I and statement II are correct
options.2: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
options.3: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
options.4: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct

brief_explanation: Statement I is incorrect; G with a line below it (G) indicates a superior ovary, while a line above it indicates an inferior ovary. Statement II correctly identifies ⊕ as actinomorphic and G as superior ovary.

subject: Biology
question: Streptokinase produced by bacterium Streptococcus is used for
brief_explanation: Streptokinase is used as a 'clot buster' (thrombolytic medication) to break down clots in blood vessels, particularly after a myocardial infarction (heart attack).

subject: Biology
question: Which chromosome in the human genome has the highest number of genes?
brief_explanation: As per the findings of the Human Genome Project, Chromosome 1 is the largest human chromosome and has the highest number of genes.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following statement is correct about location of the male frog copulatory pad?

options.1: First and Second digit of fore limb
options.4: First digit of the fore limb

brief_explanation: The copulatory pad, a secondary sexual characteristic in male frogs used to grasp the female during amplexus, is located on the first digit (thumb) of the forelimb.

subject: Biology
question: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
brief_explanation: Cytokinins are known to promote nutrient mobilization to the areas where they are applied, which helps in delaying leaf senescence (the Richmond-Lang effect).

subject: Biology
question: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal?
brief_explanation: This describes a pseudocoelom, where the body cavity is not completely lined by mesoderm. The mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm, lining only the body wall side.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-The head of the sperm contains the genetic material (nucleus). B-The middle piece is packed with mitochondria, providing energy for movement. C-The acrosome is a cap-like structure containing enzymes for fertilization. D-The tail is responsible for sperm motility.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence. A. Prothallus stage B. Meiosis in spore mother cells C. Fertilisation D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte. E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water.
brief_explanation: The correct sequence is: B (Sporophyte undergoes meiosis to produce spores) -> A (Spores germinate into prothallus/gametophyte) -> D (Gametophyte forms sex organs) -> E (Gamete transfer via water) -> C (Fertilization to form a zygote, which grows into a new sporophyte).

subject: Biology
question: Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by: A. Nodal tissue B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata C. Adrenal medullary hormones D. Adrenal cortical hormones
brief_explanation: The heart's activity is intrinsically regulated by nodal tissue (A), extrinsically modulated by the neural center in the medulla oblongata (B), and also influenced by adrenal medullary hormones like adrenaline (C). Adrenal cortical hormones are not directly involved in regulating cardiac activity.

subject: Biology
question: Which of following organisms cannot fix nitrogen?
statements: A. Azotobacter
B. Oscillatoria
C. Anabaena
D. Volvox
E. Nostoc
brief_explanation: Azotobacter, Oscillatoria, Anabaena, and Nostoc are all known nitrogen-fixing organisms (prokaryotes). Volvox is a colonial green alga (eukaryote) and does not fix atmospheric nitrogen.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA. Statement II: RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.

options.1: Both statement I and statement II are correct
options.2: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
options.3: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
options.4: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct

brief_explanation: Statement I is incorrect; both tRNA (via anticodon) and rRNA (as part of the ribosome) are essential for interacting with mRNA during translation. Statement II is correct; RNAi is a conserved mechanism of gene silencing in eukaryotes.

subject: Biology
question: In the above represented plasmid an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies?

options.1: Using ampicillin & tetracyclin containing medium plate.
options.2: Blue color colonies will be selected.
options.3: White color colonies will be selected.
options.4: Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.

brief_explanation: The plasmid shows blue-white screening. The EcoRI site is within the lacZ (β-galactosidase) gene. Insertion of DNA at this site disrupts the gene (insertional inactivation), so bacteria with recombinant plasmids cannot produce a functional enzyme and will form white colonies on a medium containing X-gal.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
brief_explanation: Eli Lilly, an American company, first produced human insulin (Humulin) in 1983 using recombinant DNA technology by inserting the genes for the A and B chains into plasmids of the bacterium Escherichia coli.

subject: Biology
question: Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction: S-G + S' → S + S' - G Where, G→ a group other than hydrogen, S→ a substrate, S' → another substrate
brief_explanation: The reaction shows the transfer of a functional group (G) from one substrate (S) to another (S'). Enzymes that catalyze this type of reaction belong to the class Transferases.

subject: Biology
question: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.

options.3: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.

brief_explanation: A characteristic feature of a monocot stem is that its hypodermis is made of sclerenchymatous tissue, not parenchymatous tissue. The other three statements are correct features of a monocot stem.

subject: Biology
question: The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is
statements: A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg.
B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum.
C. Reduction division to produce haploid spores.
D. Formation of sporophyte.
E. Release of antherozoids into water.
brief_explanation: The bryophyte life cycle starting from a gametophyte is: B (Attachment) -> E (Antherozoid release) -> A (Fertilization) -> D (Zygote develops into Sporophyte) -> C (Sporophyte produces spores via meiosis).

subject: Biology
question: Which are correct: A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs. B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells. C. α-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour. D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers. E. In the case of leukaemia blood cells counts are decreased.
brief_explanation: CT and MRI are used for cancer detection (A is correct). Chemo drugs kill cancerous cells (B is incorrect). α-interferon is a biological response modifier that activates the immune system (C is correct). Chemo drugs are chemicals, not BRMs (D is incorrect). Leukemia involves an increase in blood cell counts (E is incorrect).

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Centromere is the primary constriction of a chromosome, essential for cell division. B-Cilium is involved in cell movement. C-Cristae are the infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane. D-The cell membrane is primarily a phospholipid bilayer.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Chlorophyll a is blue-green. B-Chlorophyll b is yellow-green. C-Xanthophylls are yellow. D-Carotenoids are yellow to yellow-orange.

subject: Biology
question: Find the correct statements:
statements: A. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks.
B. In human pregnancy the major organ systems are formed at the end of 8 weeks.
C. In human pregnancy heart is formed after one month of gestation.
D. In human pregnancy, limbs and digits develop by the end of second month.
E. In human pregnancy the appearance of hair usually observed in the fifth month.

options.3: B, C, D and E Only
options.4: A, C, D and E Only

brief_explanation: By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most major organ systems are formed (A is correct, B is incorrect). The heart is formed after one month (C is correct). Limbs and digits develop by the end of the second month (D is correct). Appearance of hair on the head is during the fifth month (E is correct).

subject: Biology
question: In the seeds of cereals, the outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a protein-rich layer called:
brief_explanation: The aleurone layer is a protein-rich outer layer of the endosperm in cereal grains, which separates the endosperm from the embryo.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following diagrams is correct with regard to the proximal (P) and distal (D) tubule of the Nephron.
brief_explanation: In the PCT, there is major reabsorption of HCO₃⁻ and secretion of H⁺ and NH₃. In the DCT, there is conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ (and water) and secretion of K⁺ and H⁺. Diagram (2) correctly depicts these transport processes.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the part of a bio-reactor which is used as a foam braker from the given figure.
brief_explanation: In a stirred-tank bioreactor, the foam breaker is located at the top of the agitator shaft to break any foam that forms during the culturing process. This corresponds to label C in the diagram.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): A typical unfertilized, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled. Reason (R): The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei.

options.1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.2: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.3: A is true but R is false.
options.4: A is false but R is true.

brief_explanation: Assertion (A) is true; a mature embryo sac has 3 antipodals, 1 central cell (with 2 polar nuclei), and an egg apparatus (1 egg, 2 synergids), totaling 7 cells and 8 nuclei. Reason (R) is false; the egg apparatus has one egg cell and two synergids. The two polar nuclei are in the central cell.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the set of correct statements:
statements: A. The flowers of Vallisneria are colourful and produce nectar.
B. The flowers of waterlily are not pollinated by water.
C. In most of water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting.
D. Pollen grains of some hydrophytes are long and ribbon like.
E. In some hydrophytes, the pollen grains are carried passively inside water.

options.1: A, C, D and E only
options.2: B, C, D and E only
options.4: A, B, C and D only

brief_explanation: Water-pollinated flowers (like Vallisneria) are not colorful or nectar-producing (A is false). Many aquatic plants like water lily are pollinated by insects or wind (B is correct). Pollen grains in water-pollinated species are protected by a mucilaginous cover (C is correct), can be long and ribbon-like (D is correct), and are carried passively in water (E is correct).

subject: Biology
question: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care is called:
brief_explanation: Ex-situ (off-site) conservation involves protecting threatened species outside their natural habitats, such as in zoological parks, botanical gardens, and wildlife safari parks.

subject: Biology
question: Inhibition of Succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate is a classical example of:
brief_explanation: Malonate is a structural analogue of the substrate succinate. It competes with succinate for the active site of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase, which is the definition of competitive inhibition.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the part of the seed from the given figure which is destined to form root when the seed germinates.
brief_explanation: In an embryo, the radicle develops into the root system. In the given diagram of a dicot embryo, label 'B' points to the radicle.

subject: Biology
question: Bulliform cells are responsible for:

options.2: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
options.3: Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
options.4: Protecting the plant from salt stress.

brief_explanation: Bulliform cells in monocot leaves lose turgidity during water stress, causing the leaves to curl inwards to reduce the surface area exposed to sunlight and minimize water loss via transpiration.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
statements: A. Light
B. Chlorophyll
C. CO2
D. ATP
E. NADPH
brief_explanation: The dark reaction (Calvin cycle) utilizes the products of the light reaction (ATP and NADPH) to fix atmospheric CO₂ into carbohydrates. Light and chlorophyll are required for the light reaction, not directly for the dark reaction.

subject: Biology
question: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example for:
brief_explanation: Dedifferentiation is the process by which permanent, differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide and become meristematic, as seen in the formation of interfascicular cambium.

subject: Biology
question: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of:
brief_explanation: The restriction endonuclease Hind II was the first to be characterized and its specific recognition sequence is six base pairs long.

subject: Biology
question: Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because:
statements: A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years...
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.

options.3: A, C, D and E only
options.4: A, B, C and D only

brief_explanation: Tropical regions have high biodiversity due to long evolutionary stability (A), high solar energy and productivity (C), and a constant, less seasonal environment that promotes niche specialization (D, E). Tropical environments are less, not more, seasonal (B is incorrect).

subject: Biology
question: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
brief_explanation: The kingdom Fungi is divided into various classes primarily based on morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation, and the type of fruiting body. Mode of nutrition is a characteristic of the kingdom as a whole, not a primary criterion for classification within it.

subject: Biology
question: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO2 fixed in the Calvin cycle?

options.1: 3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
options.2: 3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
options.3: 2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
options.4: 2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH

brief_explanation: For the fixation of one molecule of CO₂ in the Calvin cycle, 2 ATP and 2 NADPH are used in the reduction step, and 1 ATP is used in the regeneration step. This totals 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.

subject: Biology
question: These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss:
statements: A. Over exploitation
B. Co-extinction
C. Mutation
D. Habitat loss and fragmentation
E. Migration

options.4: A, B, C and D only

brief_explanation: The major causes for biodiversity loss are known as 'The Evil Quartet': Habitat loss and fragmentation (D), Over-exploitation (A), Alien species invasions, and Co-extinctions (B).

subject: Biology
question: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called:
brief_explanation: Totipotency is the inherent potential of a plant cell to grow and develop into a whole plant. It is the principle behind micropropagation.

subject: Biology
question: The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is dN/dt = rN((K-N)/K). From this equation, K indicates:
brief_explanation: In the logistic growth equation, K represents the carrying capacity of the environment, which is the maximum population size that can be sustained by the available resources.

subject: Biology
question: Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores of chromosomes during:
brief_explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, and spindle fibers from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores located on the centromeres.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (a) and (b).
brief_explanation: Figure (a) shows a superior ovary with other parts arising below it, which is a hypogynous flower. Figure (b) shows an inferior ovary with other parts arising above it, which is an epigynous flower.

subject: Biology
question: Match List I with List II:
brief_explanation: A-Rhizopus is the common bread mould. B-Ustilago causes smut disease. C-Puccinia causes rust disease. D-Agaricus is the genus for common mushrooms.

subject: Biology
question: In a plant, black seed color (BB/Bb) is dominant over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, with which of the following genotype will you cross it?
brief_explanation: This describes a test cross, where an individual with a dominant phenotype (unknown genotype) is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual (bb) to determine its genotype.

subject: Biology
question: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?

options.2: Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
options.4: Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants

brief_explanation: This is a case of incomplete dominance. A pink flower is heterozygous (Rr) and a red flower is homozygous dominant (RR). The cross Rr x RR yields offspring with genotypes RR (red) and Rr (pink) in a 1:1 ratio.

subject: Biology
question: Match List I with List II:

statements.List I: A. Two or more alternative forms of a gene
B. Cross of F1 progeny with homozygous recessive parent
C. Cross of F1 progeny with any of the parents
D. Number of chromosome sets in plant

brief_explanation: A-Alternative forms of a gene are called alleles. B-A cross of F1 with a homozygous recessive parent is a test cross. C-A cross of F1 with any parent is a back cross. D-The number of chromosome sets is ploidy.

subject: Biology
question: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
brief_explanation: Lecithin is a type of phospholipid, a class of lipids that are a major component of all cell membranes. It contains a phosphate group.

subject: Biology
question: Match List I with List II:
brief_explanation: A-Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid. B-Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) produces ethanol. C-Trichoderma polysporum produces the immunosuppressant cyclosporin-A. D-Streptococcus produces the clot-buster streptokinase.

subject: Biology
question: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls?
brief_explanation: The figure shows a transverse section of an anther. Label 'C' points to the endothecium layer, whose cells have thin outer walls and thickened inner walls, which aid in anther dehiscence.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following is an example of actinomorphic flower?
brief_explanation: Actinomorphic flowers exhibit radial symmetry. Datura is an example from the Solanaceae family with actinomorphic flowers. Pisum, Sesbania, and Cassia have zygomorphic (bilateral symmetry) flowers.

subject: Biology
question: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in DNA and these are with respect to upstream and down stream end:
brief_explanation: A standard transcription unit in DNA consists of three main regions: a promoter (where transcription starts), the structural gene (which is transcribed), and a terminator (where transcription ends).

subject: Biology
question: What is the fate of piece of DNA carrying only gene of interest which is transferred into an alien organism?
statements: A. The piece of DNA would be able to multiply itself independently in the progeny cells of the organisms.
B. It may get integrated into the genome of the recipient.
C. It may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
D. The alien piece of DNA is not an integrated part of chromosome.
E. It shows ability to replicate.
brief_explanation: A piece of foreign DNA without an origin of replication cannot replicate independently (A and E are false). For it to be inherited, it must integrate into the host genome (B is correct), after which it will be replicated and passed on along with the host's DNA (C is correct).

subject: Biology
question: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin:

options.1: does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
options.2: can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth.
options.4: promotes abscission of mature leaves only.

brief_explanation: Synthetic auxins like 2,4-D are widely used as herbicides to kill dicotyledonous weeds but do not affect mature monocotyledonous plants like grasses, making them effective for maintaining weed-free lawns.

subject: Biology
question: The cofactor of the enzyme carboxypeptidase is:
brief_explanation: Carboxypeptidase is a metalloenzyme that requires a metal ion for its activity. The specific metal ion that acts as a cofactor for carboxypeptidase is Zinc (Zn²⁺).

subject: Biology
question: The lactose present in the growth medium of bacteria is transported to the cell by the action of
brief_explanation: In the lac operon, the product of the 'y' gene is permease, an enzyme that increases the permeability of the cell membrane to lactose, allowing it to be transported into the cell.

subject: Biology
question: Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
statements: A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive.
B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in F2 generation.
C. Factors occur in pair in normal diploid plants.
D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor.
E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross.

options.2: A, B, C, D and E
options.4: A, C, D and E only

brief_explanation: The Law of Dominance explains that characters are controlled by factors (D), which occur in pairs (C), and in a dissimilar pair, one member (dominant) expresses itself over the other (recessive) (A). This leads to the F1 hybrid expressing only one parental character (E). Statement B describes segregation, not dominance.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Bt toxins are insect group specific and coded by a gene cry IAc. Statement II: Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in B. thuringiensis. However, after ingested by the insect the inactive protoxin gets converted into active form due to acidic pH of the insect gut.

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

brief_explanation: Statement I is correct; Bt toxins are specific, and genes like cryIAc code for them. Statement II is incorrect because the inactive protoxin is activated by the alkaline pH of the insect's gut, not acidic pH.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue. Statement II: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.

options.1: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

brief_explanation: Statement I is incorrect because both parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues; sclerenchyma is dead. Statement II is correct; gymnosperms have tracheids but lack vessels, while vessels are a key feature of angiosperm xylem.

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two Statements: Statement I: Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage. Statement II: The beginning of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Statement I is true but statement II is false.
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.3: Both statement I and Statement II are true.
options.4: Both statement I and Statement II are false.

brief_explanation: Statement I is correct; chromosomes start to condense and become visible during the leptotene stage of Prophase I. Statement II is also correct; the diplotene stage is characterized by the breakdown of the synaptonemal complex and separation of homologous chromosomes, which remain attached at chiasmata.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.

statements.List-II: (III) Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis

brief_explanation: A-Nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis. B-Centrioles have a characteristic 'cartwheel' organization. C-Leucoplasts are colorless plastids used for storing nutrients. D-Golgi apparatus is involved in the formation of glycolipids and glycoproteins.

subject: Biology
question: List of endangered spb&ies was released by:
brief_explanation: The IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature) maintains and publishes the Red List of Threatened Species, which is a comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of species.

subject: Biology
question: The DNA present in chloroplast is:
brief_explanation: Similar to mitochondria and prokaryotes, chloroplasts contain their own genetic material in the form of a small, circular, double-stranded DNA molecule.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following are fused in somatic hybridization involving two varieties of plants?
brief_explanation: Somatic hybridization is a technique that involves the fusion of isolated protoplasts (plant cells with their cell walls removed) from two different plant varieties or species.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the correct description about the given figure:

options.3: Wind pollinated plant inflorescence showing flowers with well-exposed stamens.
options.4: Water pollinated flowers showing stamens with mucilaginous covering.

brief_explanation: The figure shows a compact inflorescence with large, feathery stigmas and well-exposed stamens, which are characteristic adaptations for anemophily or wind pollination.

subject: Biology
question: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield?
brief_explanation: Gibberellins are known to promote stem and internode elongation. Spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellin increases the stem length, thereby increasing the yield of sugar.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Frederick Griffith discovered the principle of bacterial transformation. B-Jacob and Monod proposed the Lac operon model for gene regulation. C-Har Gobind Khorana made significant contributions to deciphering the genetic code. D-Meselson and Stahl experimentally proved the semi-conservative mode of DNA replication.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II
brief_explanation: A-GLUT-4 is a protein transporter that enables glucose to enter cells. B-Insulin is a hormone. C-Trypsin is a digestive enzyme. D-Collagen is the main protein of intercellular ground substance (connective tissue).

subject: Biology
question: Given below are two statements. Statement I: In C4 Plants, some O2 binds RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased. Statement II: In C4 Plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

brief_explanation: Statement I is false because C4 plants have a mechanism to concentrate CO₂, preventing O₂ from binding to RuBisCO and thus avoiding decreased CO₂ fixation. Statement II is also false; mesophyll cells do not perform the Calvin cycle (and thus no photorespiration), while the CO₂ concentrating mechanism prevents photorespiration in bundle sheath cells.

subject: Biology
question: Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
brief_explanation: The conversion of Succinyl-CoA to Succinic acid is a substrate-level phosphorylation step that generates GTP (or ATP). It does not involve oxidation (i.e., removal of hydrogen/electrons) of the substrate.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Citric acid (Krebs) cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix. B-Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm. C-The Electron transport system is located on the inner mitochondrial membrane. D-The Proton gradient is built up in the intermembrane space.

subject: Biology
question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the process of replication in E.coli?

options.1: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5'→3' direction.
options.2: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5'→3' and 3'→5' direction.
options.3: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction, that is 3'→5'.
options.4: The DNA dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction, that is 5'→3'.

brief_explanation: DNA polymerase, the enzyme responsible for DNA replication, can only add new nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing DNA strand. Therefore, it always synthesizes the new strand in the 5' to 3' direction.

subject: Biology
question: In an ecosystem if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is 100x(kcal m⁻²)yr⁻¹ what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem?
brief_explanation: This question is likely flawed as it asks for GPP of T3 from NPP of T1. Assuming it asks for the energy available at T3: Following the 10% law, energy at T2 is 10% of 100x = 10x. Energy at T3 is 10% of 10x = x. The Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total production at the first trophic level, but the question asks for the GPP of the third trophic level, which is not a standard term. The energy available at T3 is 'x'.

subject: Biology
question: Match List-I with List-II.
brief_explanation: A-Rose has perigynous flowers. B-Pea has marginal placentation. C-Cotton shows twisted aestivation in its corolla. D-Mango is a type of fruit called a drupe.

subject: Biology
